correctness.rationale: Normal ordering the full displacement operator gives the stated Laguerre matrix elements. After removing the nonzero Gaussian and r^m factors, harmonic m>0 is an arbitrary complex polynomial of degree <=N-m, and harmonic zero is a real polynomial of degree <=N with its value at zero fixed by the trace. For traceless differences and Q(x)=product_j(x-r_j^2), the invisible polynomials are exactly multiples of Q for m>0 and xQ for m=0. Counting the real dimensions gives (N+1-min(K,N))^2-1, including K=0 and N=0. Any nonzero blind direction can perturb the maximally mixed state in both signs while preserving strict positivity. At positive radius and N>=1 the constant harmonic can be varied (the difference L_0(x)-L_1(x) is x), and the N complex harmonics vary independently, giving dimension 2N+1. Fewer than N+1 complex samples cannot separate these traces, and the proposed half-circle grid gives a full 2N+2-point Fourier grid by conjugacy, hence suffices.
residual_risks: Exact noiseless complex Weyl data and known trace only; exponentiating the truncated annihilation matrix would not give the same model. The angular lower bound is for each circle on its own, not for the joint optimization of total samples.
